evals.prompt: We ran an A/B test on our pricing page for 4 weeks. Control: 2.1% conversion. Variant: 2.4% conversion. 12,000 visitors per variant. Is this statistically significant? Should we ship it?
evals.expected_output: Should calculate the result under a declared analysis: 252/12,000 vs 288/12,000 gives approximately p = 0.117 for an uncorrected two-sided pooled-proportion z-test, so it does not meet alpha = 0.05. Should distinguish the 0.3 percentage-point / ~14% relative estimate from evidence for a reliably positive effect. Report uncertainty and practical business impact. Respect the pre-specified duration and stopping rule; do not recommend continuing the completed fixed-horizon test until significant. Unplanned segments are exploratory; a follow-up test needs its own plan.
assertions: Uses actual conversion counts and states the analysis assumptions
Does not call p ~0.117 significant at alpha = 0.05
Distinguishes statistical uncertainty from business value
Does not extend a completed fixed-horizon test until significant

evals.prompt: Our fixed-horizon A/B test reached its planned sample today with p = 0.04. Can I tell the CEO there is a 96% chance the change works and just a 4% chance the lift was random? We have a +2% estimate, an interval of +0.1% to +3.9%, and a higher refund rate in the variant.
evals.expected_output: Reject both probability interpretations. Explain the p-value conditional on the null model and assumptions, and repeated-sampling interval coverage without asserting a posterior probability. Consider the effect interval, practical impact and refund guardrail before recommending rollout. Do not substitute a numerical significance threshold for the business decision.
assertions: Does not interpret 1-p as the probability the variant works
Does not interpret p as the probability the result was random
Uses interval, business effect and refund guardrail before rollout
